documents.embed_text: Core errata 2.1.1: Access permission faults are prioritized over unaligned device memory faults. A load or store which causes an unaligned access to device memory results in an UNALIGNED UsageFault exception. However, if the region is not accessible because of the MPU access permissions (as specified in MPU_RBAR.AP), then the resulting MemManage fault is prioritized over the UsageFault. The failure occurs when the MPU is enabled and: a load/store access occurs to an address which is not aligned to the data type specified in the instruction; the memory access hits one region only; the region attributes (MAIR register) mark the location as device memory; the region access permissions prevent the access (unprivileged or write not allowed). Workaround: None. However, it is expected that no existing software is relying on this behavior since it was permitted in Armv7-M.

documents.embed_text: System errata 2.2.1: Low-speed external clock in analog bypass mode might not work properly. While the LSE bypass in analog mode is selected (LSEBYP = 1 and LSEEXT = 0 in the RCC_BDCR register), the LSE clock might not work properly. Workaround: Do not use the LSE bypass in analog mode. Instead, use the digital LSE bypass mode (LSEBYP = 1 and LSEEXT = 1 in the RCC_BDCR register).

documents.embed_text: System errata 2.2.2: LSE crystal oscillator may be disturbed by transitions on PC13. On LQFP packages, the LSE crystal oscillator clock frequency can be incorrect when PC13 is toggling in input or output (for example when used for RTC_OUT1). The external clock input (LSE bypass) is not impacted by this limitation. The WLCSP and UFBGA packages are not impacted by this limitation. Avoid toggling PC13 when LSE is used on LQFP packages. Workaround: None.

documents.embed_text: ADC errata 2.3.1: In simultaneous regular mode, stopping an injected conversion may shift the next regular conversion master and slave timing by one clock cycle. In simultaneous regular mode (DUAL[4:0] = 0x06 in the ADCC_CCR register), injected conversions can be activated either on ADC1 or ADC2. When regular conversions are ongoing, if an injected conversion stop (JADSTP) occurs at the same time as an injected trigger event, then ADC1 and ADC2 timing may be shifted by one clock cycle. Workaround: Apply one of the following measures: avoid triggering injected conversions, stopping injected conversions, and enabling regular conversion in simultaneous regular mode from occurring simultaneously; stop regular conversions before stopping injected conversions; stop injected trigger source before stopping injected conversions; or configure DUAL[4:0] to 0x01 or 0x02.

documents.embed_text: ADC errata 2.3.2: Injected conversions do not work when SMPTRIG bit is set, regular conversions start then stop, and SMPTRIG bit is cleared. Injected conversions do not work after the following sequence: the SMPTRIG bit of the ADC_CFGR2 register is set (sampling time control trigger mode enabled); regular conversions are started then stopped; the SMPTRIG is cleared. Workaround: If SMPTRIG is set, disable the ADC, clear the SMPTRIG, and enable again the ADC before starting injected conversions.

documents.embed_text: RNG errata 2.5.1: RNG may report continuous seed errors in specific environmental conditions. Under certain combinations of supply voltage, temperature, and process variation, one of the RNG analog noise sources may provide insufficient entropy. As a consequence, the RNG generates seed errors continuously. If the application correctly implements the error handling procedure described in the Error Management section of the RNG chapter, it can reliably detect this condition and recover from continuous seed error generation. Workaround: No application workaround is required or applicable as it is handled by the standard error management procedure.

documents.embed_text: LPTIM errata 2.6.1: Device may remain stuck in LPTIM interrupt when entering Stop mode. This limitation occurs when disabling the low-power timer (LPTIM). When the user application clears the ENABLE bit in the LPTIM_CR register within a small time window around one LPTIM interrupt occurrence, the LPTIM interrupt signal used to wake up the device from Stop mode may be frozen in active state, preventing the device from entering low-power mode. This applies to all Stop modes and all LPTIM instances. Occurrence of this issue is very low. Workaround: In order to disable a low power timer (LPTIMx) peripheral, do not clear its ENABLE bit in its respective LPTIM_CR register. Instead, reset the whole LPTIMx peripheral via the RCC controller by setting and resetting its respective LPTIMxRST bit in the relevant RCC register.

documents.embed_text: LPTIM errata 2.6.2: ARRM and CMPM flags are not set when APB clock is slower than kernel clock. When LPTIM is configured in one shot mode and APB clock is lower than kernel clock, ARRM and CMPM flags may not be set at the end of the counting cycle defined by the repetition value REP[7:0]. This can only occur when the repetition counter is configured with an odd repetition value. Workaround: Respect the formula: {ARR, CMP} >= KER_CLK / (2 * APB_CLK), where APB_CLK is the LPTIM APB clock frequency and KER_CLK is the LPTIM kernel clock frequency (ARR and CMP expressed in decimal value).

documents.embed_text: RTC errata 2.7.1: Alarm flag may be repeatedly set when the core is stopped in debug. When the core is stopped in debug mode, clock is still supplied to the subsecond RTC alarm downcounter even when the device is configured to stop the RTC in debug. When the subsecond counter is used for the alarm condition and the alarm condition is met just before entering a breakpoint or printf, the ALRAF and/or ALRBF flag of RTC_SR is repeatedly set by hardware during the breakpoint, making any attempt to clear the flag ineffective. Workaround: None.

documents.embed_text: RTC errata 2.7.2: RTC calendar read may return transient incorrect value when BYPSHAD = 0. When the BYPSHAD control bit in RTC_CR is cleared, reading the RTC calendar registers (RTC_SSR, RTC_TR, RTC_DR) may seldom produce incorrect values, because internal timing can cause the asynchronous RTC calendar registers to be copied into shadow registers during a transition. Any erroneous value persists for only one RTC kernel clock cycle; likelihood is very low. Workaround: Set the BYPSHAD control bit to 1 in RTC_CR to bypass shadow registers, or read the RTC calendar registers twice and compare the two readings, repeating until two consecutive readings match.

documents.embed_text: RTC errata 2.7.3: System stuck if some RTC or TAMP registers are written when write protection is enabled. The system becomes stuck if some RTC or TAMP register bits are written to 1 while write protection is enabled in the PWR controller. The bits creating the failure are: any bit of RTC_SCR, any bit of TAMP_SCR, and the BKERASE bit of TAMP_CR2. Does not occur if the software sequence described in the reference manual is correctly executed. Workaround: None. Only a system reset can recover from this stuck state.

documents.embed_text: I2C errata 2.8.1: Wrong data sampling when data setup time (tSU;DAT) is shorter than one I2C kernel clock period. The I2C-bus specification requires a minimum data setup time (tSU;DAT): 250 ns in Standard mode, 100 ns in Fast mode, 50 ns in Fast mode Plus. The device does not correctly sample the I2C-bus SDA line when tSU;DAT is smaller than one I2C kernel clock period: the previous SDA value is sampled instead of the current one, which can cause wrong receipt of target address, data byte, or acknowledge bit. Workaround: Increase the I2C kernel clock frequency so its period fits within the transmitter's minimum data setup time (or increase the transmitter's minimum data setup time). With standard I2C-bus minimum setup times: Standard mode needs I2CCLK >= 4 MHz, Fast mode needs I2CCLK >= 10 MHz, Fast-mode Plus needs I2CCLK >= 20 MHz.

documents.embed_text: I2C errata 2.8.2: Spurious bus error detection in controller mode. In controller mode, a bus error can be detected spuriously, setting the BERR flag of I2C_SR and generating a bus error interrupt if enabled. Detection has no effect on the ongoing I2C-bus transfer, which continues normally. Workaround: If a bus error interrupt is generated in controller mode, clear the BERR flag by software. No other action is required.

When the ONEBIT bit is set in USART_CR3 (one sample bit method used), the noise error (NE) flag must remain cleared, but is instead set upon noise detection on the START bit. Having noise on the START bit is contradictory with using the one sample bit method in a noise-free environment. Workaround: None.

documents.embed_text: LPUART errata 2.10.1: Possible LPUART transmitter issue when using low BRR[15:0] value. The LPUART transmitter bit length sequence is not reset between consecutive bytes, which can cause jitter that the receiver cannot handle, leading to desynchronization and data corruption. This happens when the ratio between the LPUART kernel clock and the baud rate (BRR[15:0]) is not an integer and is in the three to four range, e.g. a 32.768 kHz kernel clock with a 9600 baud rate (ratio 3.41). Workaround: Increase the ratio between the LPUART kernel clock and the baud rate on the transmitter side (higher kernel clock or lower baud rate), or generate the baud rate on the receiver side using a higher frequency with oversampling if supported.

documents.embed_text: FDCAN errata 2.12.1: Desynchronization under specific condition with edge filtering enabled. FDCAN may desynchronize and incorrectly receive the first bit of the frame if edge filtering is enabled (EFBI bit of FDCAN_CCCR set) and the end of the integration phase coincides with a falling edge on FDCAN_Rx. The CRC then flags the received frame as faulty and an error frame is sent. This does not affect the reception of standard frames. Workaround: Disable edge filtering or wait for frame retransmission.

documents.embed_text: FDCAN errata 2.12.2: Tx FIFO messages inverted under specific buffer usage and priority setting. Two consecutive messages from the Tx FIFO may be inverted in the transmit sequence if FDCAN uses both a dedicated Tx buffer and a Tx FIFO (TFQM bit of FDCAN_TXBC cleared), and the messages in the Tx buffer have higher internal CAN priority than the messages in the Tx FIFO. Workaround: Apply one of: ensure only one Tx FIFO element is pending for transmission at any time; use only a Tx FIFO for both messages; or use two dedicated Tx buffers instead of the Tx FIFO.

documents.embed_text: Workaround for FDCAN issue - Tx FIFO messages inverted under specific buffer usage and priority setting: Apply one of: ensure only one Tx FIFO element is pending for transmission at any time; use only a Tx FIFO for both messages; or use two dedicated Tx buffers instead of the Tx FIFO.

documents.embed_text: USB errata 2.13.1: Buffer description table update completes after CTR interrupt triggers. During OUT transfers, the correct transfer interrupt (CTR) is triggered slightly before the last USB SRAM accesses complete. If software responds quickly to the interrupt, the full buffer contents may not yet be correct. Workaround: Include a small delay before accessing the SRAM contents: 800 ns in Full Speed mode, 6.4 us in Low Speed mode.
